applies_why: This judge text treats earlier-round section [CR2] G as answering the almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows and leaves the link underdetermined rather than counting those rows as unanswered witnesses.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] G answers the 'almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows, leaving the sign's sense open.
rule_words: A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. If the judge says a verse was answered, the judge must not count it. Not counting it obeys this rule.
room: 'If the judge says a verse was answered, the judge must not count it': either the judge must expressly say it is not counted, or it is enough that the judge calls the rows answered and does not count them; this text does the latter.
why: The judge text says [CR2] G answers the relevant rows and leaves the sign's sense open, so it does not count an answered verse as an unanswered witness and therefore obeys K-G4.
